title: Studio page composition
question: How should the Studio (/about) page be structured? The visual world stays Parchment Atelier — this choice is composition only.

options.label: Split Atelier Dialogue
options.thesis: A continuous studio story on one side; photography and people answer on the other as you scroll.
options.viewport: After the solid nav: large Studio title left, one-line Marbella/2009 meta; a tall founder plate begins immediately on the right — no card stack, no stats.
options.risk: Can feel like two pages if the columns never meet; the story and plates must share one scroll rhythm.

options.label: Values Ladder
options.thesis: Studio beliefs climb a vertical spine; team portraits nest between the rungs as living proof.
options.viewport: Full-width Studio headline, one support line, then the first ladder rung (Schedule/Team belief) with a portrait inset — no hero card grid.
options.risk: Reads like Work scheme if the spine feels too process-heavy; keep it belief, not procedure.

options.label: Founder-Led Atelier
options.thesis: The founder portrait and quote are the first belief; the team and studio story arrive as proof afterward.
options.viewport: Thin Studio wordmark line, then a dominant 4/5 founder plate with name, role, and quote beside — brand calm, person large.
options.risk: Can over-center one person if the team section feels bolted on; keep the handoff to people intentional.

options.label: Plate Section Credits
options.thesis: Team as a design-annual plate section: registration corners, credit rows, one continuous sheet of people.
options.viewport: Studio title as plate header; first team plate with corner marks and a credit row under — story deferred below the fold.
options.case: Strong craft clarity for a design studio; loses narrowly because villa owners need the studio story before a credits sheet.
options.risk: Can feel too graphic-design-insider if registration furniture overpowers warmth.

options.label: Fold Sequence Story
options.thesis: The studio story unfolds in discrete creases — each fold reveals belief, founder, then people.
options.viewport: Fold 01 marker + one large typographic crease (process clarity claim); no photo until fold 02.
options.case: Donates sequential commitment; loses on audience ID — villa owners want people and place sooner.
options.risk: Collides with Work scheme’s step spine if numbering feels procedural.
options.kept: Discrete recoverable steps with one active crease.

options.label: Glaze Shelf Row
options.thesis: People as kiln samples in one shelf row — gravity sets reading order.
options.case: Fuses poorly: villa owners do not identify with kiln-shelf comparison.
options.kept: One horizontal proof row with gravity-led hierarchy.
options.viewport: A single horizontal row of team plates as samples.
